summary: Size export candidates with subactor/ticket-radar when installed

delivery.outcome: Add `monag export --radar`: when subactor/ticket-radar is installed on PATH, size each candidate (complexity, score, time estimate, split recommendation) via its deterministic JSON stdin/stdout interface. A missing binary or a per-candidate failure leaves that candidate unsized (radar: null) with an explicit error, never a guessed size. Off by default -- monag's behavior is unchanged unless --radar is passed.
nonGoals: monag does not vendor, install, or require ticket-radar; it is an optional external tool.
No change to what counts as a candidate (audit/catalog logic untouched) -- only sizing is added.
No write access to ticket-radar's own output (SVG/PNG visualizations) beyond the compact JSON fields already useful in a text report.

architecture.decision: Add radar_available()/run_radar()/radar_assess() to src/monag/export.py; run_radar() is a small, directly mockable subprocess boundary (monitor.command() has no stdin support, needed here). Wire a new --radar flag on the export subcommand; no new runtime dependency since ticket-radar is invoked as an external binary, not imported.
architecture.rollback: Revert the application slice through protected review.

validation.evidence: Radar enrichment (available/missing/per-candidate-failure) and CLI wiring regression suite passes.
